faqs.question: What does the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis or Non-tuberculous Mycobacteria (NTM) in body fluid samples.

faqs.question: Why is the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test done?
faqs.answer: This test is done to • Diagnose infections caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis or NTM. • Monitor the effectiveness of treatment for tuberculosis. • Identify the presence of other mycobacterial infections.

faqs.question: When is the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended if you • Have symptoms suggestive of tuberculosis, such as persistent cough, weight loss, fever, and night sweats. • Have been exposed to someone with tuberculosis. • Have a weakened immune system. • Are being treated for tuberculosis and need monitoring.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate an active infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis or other non-tuberculous mycobacteria.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test?
faqs.answer: During this test, a 2ml sample of your body fluids will be collected in a sterile container and it will be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • Ensure that the specimen type, site, and proper clinical history are mentioned on the Test Request Form (TRF). • Collect 2ml of body fluid in a sterile container. • Follow any fasting or medication instructions given by your doctor. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test include: • AFB Smear Microscopy: This test quickly identifies acid-fast bacilli in clinical samples. • GeneXpert MTB/RIF Assay: This molecular test detects the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and drug resistance. • Chest X-ray: Imaging test used to detect abnormalities in the lungs suggestive of tuberculosis infection.

faqs.question: What is the AFB Rapid Culture by MGIT – Body Fluid test also known as?
faqs.answer: Acid-Fast Bacillus Rapid Culture by Mycobacteria Growth Indicator Tube

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body. Symptoms include cough, weight loss, and fatigue.
